description:
## Problem
A user starting TPC data or query generation at a large scale cannot tell how long it will take. Estimates exist today but are not measured for generation: the interactive prompt scales a per-benchmark minutes range by `(0.5 + 0.5 * scale)` (cli/benchmarks.py:708-711) and the dry run shows estimates (cli/dryrun.py:276-278,737-738).

## Change
1. Measurement runs, approved by the owner on 2026-11-21, on this Mac, one at a time through `make heavy-run`, each recording wall time and peak memory: `dsqgen` all 99 queries, timed per query, at SF 1, 100, 1000, 3000, 5000; `dsdgen` full generation at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10; `dbgen` full generation at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10. Run folders under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs are kept.
2. Put the table in the pull request and on this item.
3. Print an estimate before generation, labelled rough, naming the scales and host class it was measured on, and marking any scale above the measured ones as extrapolated. Say in the pull request how it relates to the two existing estimates (replace or feed them; one convention, not a third).
4. A run warns when its run limit is shorter than the estimate; no warning when no limit is set or the limit is larger.

## Decision gates
A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). The measured figures may be committed without a stop (owner, 2026-11-21: "Approve the runs now, and let the session commit the measured figures; the table is in the pull request and the final report."). Texts, verbatim: estimate "Rough estimate: generation will take about {estimate} (measured on {host_class} at scale {scales}{extrapolated_note})."; warning "The run limit of {limit} seconds is shorter than the estimated generation time of about {estimate}." Known so far, darwin-arm64 only: dsqgen query 9 about 5 s at SF 3000 and 11 to 13 s at SF 5000. If a measurement run is refused admission or would breach the disk floor, stop and report; do not shrink the list silently.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the measured table is recorded here with heavy-run log paths; tests assert both owner texts verbatim; tests show the printed estimate for a measured scale lies within the measured range and that an unmeasured scale is labelled extrapolated; tests show the warning when the limit is below the estimate and none when it is unset or above; `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
